## Before you start

- **Designed for:** learners with little or no programming experience.
- **You are ready when:** you can use a web browser and are willing to predict,
  run, explain, and change small examples. No mathematics prerequisite is
  assumed.
- **Practice setup:** start with generated Colab notebooks. Unit 1 explains
  local workflows before later project units use environments and command-line
  tools.

::: {.callout-note title="Required does not mean install everything immediately"}
Local Python Tools is required because every learner should understand the
workflow and choose a practice environment deliberately. You can complete its
browser-based comparisons before installing local software, then return to the
setup steps when project-focused units begin.
:::

## What you will be able to do

- trace values through decisions, loops, collections, and functions;
- choose data structures and function boundaries that make behavior explainable;
- read tracebacks, reduce failures, validate input, and work safely with files;
- organize a repeatable project with dependencies, a CLI, tests, typing, and CI;
- use classes, iteration patterns, decorators, context managers, logging, and
  configuration when they improve the design;
- build and defend a complete Python project using tests, output, explanations,
  and debugging evidence.

## Required learning sequence

Python Foundations curriculum version 4 has **20 focused instructional units**.
Each unit starts with an Overview, continues through required lessons, and ends
with a required Unit Challenge. **Unit 21** is the final project.

| Unit | Focus | Required assessment |
|---|---|---|
| 1. [Getting Started](units/getting-started/index.qmd) | Choose a practice environment and use the course workflow deliberately. | [Challenge](units/getting-started/challenge.qmd) |
| 2. [Values, Types, and Input/Output](units/values-types-input-output/index.qmd) | Represent information with Python values and exchange text with a learner. | [Challenge](units/values-types-input-output/challenge.qmd) |
| 3. [Control Flow](units/control-flow/index.qmd) | Choose which instructions run, repeat work, and trace changing state. | [Challenge](units/control-flow/challenge.qmd) |
| 4. [Data Structures](units/data-structures/index.qmd) | Choose containers that match the relationships in your data. | [Challenge](units/data-structures/challenge.qmd) |
| 5. [Functions](units/functions/index.qmd) | Give reusable behavior a clear input, result, contract, and check. | [Challenge](units/functions/challenge.qmd) |
| 6. [Debugging](units/debugging/index.qmd) | Investigate failures from evidence instead of changing code by guesswork. | [Challenge](units/debugging/challenge.qmd) |
| 7. [Files and Structured Data](units/files/index.qmd) | Move data safely between a Python program and external files. | [Challenge](units/files/challenge.qmd) |
| 8. [Error Handling and Validation](units/error-handling-and-validation/index.qmd) | Reject invalid input clearly and handle only understood failures. | [Challenge](units/error-handling-and-validation/challenge.qmd) |
| 9. [Modules and Packages](units/modules-and-packages/index.qmd) | Split reusable Python code across importable files and package namespaces. | [Challenge](units/modules-and-packages/challenge.qmd) |
| 10. [Project Structure](units/project-structure/index.qmd) | Arrange source, tests, configuration, and documentation predictably. | [Challenge](units/project-structure/challenge.qmd) |
| 11. [Environments and Dependencies](units/environments-and-dependencies/index.qmd) | Make a project runtime isolated and reproducible. | [Challenge](units/environments-and-dependencies/challenge.qmd) |
| 12. [Command-Line Programs](units/command-line-programs/index.qmd) | Turn reusable behavior into a command with explicit arguments and output. | [Challenge](units/command-line-programs/challenge.qmd) |
| 13. [Testing](units/testing/index.qmd) | Protect observable behavior with focused automated tests. | [Challenge](units/testing/challenge.qmd) |
| 14. [Code Style and Linting](units/code-style-and-linting/index.qmd) | Use automated tools to improve consistency and reveal likely mistakes. | [Challenge](units/code-style-and-linting/challenge.qmd) |
| 15. [Typing](units/typing/index.qmd) | Document value expectations and check them before runtime. | [Challenge](units/typing/challenge.qmd) |
| 16. [Automation and CI](units/automation-and-ci/index.qmd) | Run the project quality agreement automatically before and after sharing. | [Challenge](units/automation-and-ci/challenge.qmd) |
| 17. [Object-Oriented Programming](units/object-oriented-programming/index.qmd) | Model cohesive state and behavior without hiding unnecessary complexity. | [Challenge](units/object-oriented-programming/challenge.qmd) |
| 18. [Comprehensions and Iteration](units/comprehensions-and-iteration/index.qmd) | Express transformations clearly and produce sequences eagerly or lazily. | [Challenge](units/comprehensions-and-iteration/challenge.qmd) |
| 19. [Decorators and Context Managers](units/decorators-and-context-managers/index.qmd) | Apply reusable behavior around functions and resource lifecycles. | [Challenge](units/decorators-and-context-managers/challenge.qmd) |
| 20. [Logging and Configuration](units/logging-and-configuration/index.qmd) | Separate operational evidence and settings from core program behavior. | [Challenge](units/logging-and-configuration/challenge.qmd) |

### Unit 21: [Python Foundations Project](project/index.qmd)

Integrate the complete course in one small, explainable, tested project.

## Completion requirements and assessment

Python Foundations curriculum version 4 is locally complete when you have:

1. completed all **38 required lessons**;
2. recorded all **20 required unit challenges** after meeting their checks;
3. built the required [Python Foundations Project](project/index.qmd) and
   self-assessed every rubric row as **Meets the requirement**.

The Unit 1 challenge is a methodology-and-tools readiness quiz. Unit 2 through
Unit 20 use guided practical tasks designed for one or two focused hours, with
starter contracts, progressive assertions, and tiered hints. Lesson quizzes
remain formative and do not have a stored grade. There are no optional lessons
or challenges in this course.

::: {.callout-important title="Local completion is not a verified certificate"}
The completion dashboard is a private, self-reported browser record. It does not
verify identity, submit challenge artifacts, grade the project, or issue a
certificate. A verifiable certificate remains planned as a separate service.
:::

## Practice and next step

Treat each lesson as a lab: predict, run, explain, modify, and keep evidence.
Finish each unit with its challenge while the concept is fresh, then use the
final project to connect all 20 instructional units.
